## Recovered observations

207 points (43 from F5-24; 164 from F5-25) read by two readings made separately and reconciled (batch `curves-s5-b1`, rules `docs/CURVE-READING.md (2026-10-08)`). Values are SI; the printed-unit values and the pixel coordinates on the page image are kept beside them so every point can be checked against the scan. x_read_bound and y_read_bound are reading bounds in printed units: the largest change of value over the point's pixel interval on the piecewise map, plus the location error of the two lines around it (D-025; the global calibration residual is not added, see qa/<batch>/calibration-sensitivity.md for the affine difference); x_bound_si and y_bound_si are the same in SI. They are not standard deviations.

Both readings drawn on the page image (filled circles: Claude's reading; hollow squares: Codex's; bars: pixel bounds; the canonical reading of each panel is named in the batch review). Click to enlarge.

Panel 1: No. 1 footpad of the 1/6-scale model, NASA Test No. 1.
The depth is a computed output, not a direct measurement: the report's data reduction program took the 13 tape-recorded signals every 1/1000 s and calculated the footpad's penetration by numerical integration (AM-68-1 Vol. I, Section 5.5.2, printed 5-41, PDF 321).

Panel 2: Axial load of the strut, tension positive and compression negative, as the panel's printed labels give it (the axis title names the sense of the trace's main excursion); a trace beyond the panel's 0 line changes sense.

Panel 3: Axial load of the strut, tension positive and compression negative, as the panel's printed labels give it (the axis title names the sense of the trace's main excursion); a trace beyond the panel's 0 line changes sense.
On the Strut No. 2 panel the top load label is printed -60; the panel's own sequence (0, +20, +40) and the (Tension) title make it +60, and both readings anchor that line at +60 lbf.

Panel 4: Axial load of the strut, tension positive and compression negative, as the panel's printed labels give it (the axis title names the sense of the trace's main excursion); a trace beyond the panel's 0 line changes sense.

Panel 4, strut1: the line is broken after claude sample 21: a break in the drawn line at about 0.0138 to 0.0140 s, about 4 px of the page with no ink, the line resuming about 1.5 px to the side; seen by the Claude reader and in Codex's review, confirmed on the page; the line is not drawn across it.

## Notes from the two readings

- Claude: Bendix drop No. 10 (7-18-67, test type C detail correlation) is NASA Test No. 1; the T5-2 remark prints NASA Drop No. 1 and Tests No. 1-8 McDonnell reduced. Velocity: -114.93 in. sec. in the F5-25 inset, VV -114.9 In./Sec. and Vh 0 in T5-3, VV 10 and VH 0 with no unit in T5-2, nominal ten ft/s in text 5-44 (printed teen). Release to touchdown time .298 sec (T5-3). Dr 0 printed with 46.9 pcf and phi 41 (T5-2 and T5-3) whereas soil 1 RS Loose is Dr 0 at 41.4 pcf and phi 40 in Table 2-3; soil 1 mapped by state only. Loose bed depth not printed (18 inches is printed for the RS intermediate beds only). Histories reduced from 13 tape signals at 1/1000 s (text 5-43). NASA Test No. 4 (drop 13) duplicates this condition.
- Codex: NASA Test No. 1. F5-25 gives -114.93 and 0 in./sec. T5-3 gives -114.9 and 0 In./Sec. T5-2 nominal Vv 10 and Vh 0 fps. Loose-bed fill depth, model pad diameter and run Gp unreported. Earth gravity inferred.
